headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and prompt-injection via ChatGPT Desktop’s file/clipboard/screen inputs; Whisper is local-only and does not add a direct exfiltration path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop ingests files, clipboard, screenshots, and app context, so attacker-controlled content can reach its prompt surface. Whisper only processes audio/speech and has no shared channel itself, but the pair can still be bridged by user-provided transcripts or copied outputs. No direct documented provenance filter is shown, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop reads untrusted file or clipboard content that contains instructions, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF Whisper output is copied into ChatGPT Desktop without provenance labeling, THEN malicious transcript text can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff for untrusted content.
Paste only quoted excerpts into ChatGPT Desktop.
Add a visible provenance tag before copying Whisper output.
Use separate workspaces for audio transcription and reasoning.
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering between Whisper and ChatGPT Desktop.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Whisper touches audio/speech. Even though Whisper has no network egress and ChatGPT Desktop is vendor-only, the pair can still expose sensitive audio-derived content if the same material is moved between them. The shared data path is plausible in default use, so medium fits.
conditions: IF audio or speech content contains secrets and is transcribed by Whisper, THEN copying the transcript into ChatGPT Desktop exposes that content to a vendor service.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is used on uploaded files or screenshots containing sensitive data, THEN that data may be processed outside the local environment.
mitigations: Redact secrets before transcription.
Keep sensitive audio offline from ChatGPT Desktop.
Use a local-only transcription workflow for regulated content.
Avoid uploading screenshots or files with confidential data.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before cross-agent transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Whisper cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP, and ChatGPT Desktop also cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct resource conflict is limited. The only shared mutable surface is user-mediated content transfer, which is not a write race. This is low rather than none because the pair still shares read/input channels.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same mutable external resource through a third-party orchestrator, THEN coordination issues could appear.
IF an operator manually copies outputs back and forth, THEN stale-state confusion can occur.
mitigations: Keep Whisper and ChatGPT Desktop on separate artifacts.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same file.
Use read-only transcripts for Whisper output.
Do not rely on either agent for git writes.
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared orchestrator is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can act on files and app context, while Whisper produces speech/audio transcriptions that may be treated as authoritative text. If Whisper output is fed into ChatGPT Desktop without verification, transcription errors can cascade into incorrect downstream reasoning or actions. The pair lacks an intrinsic verification step, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Whisper output is used as source text for ChatGPT Desktop without human review, THEN transcription errors can propagate.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to summarize or act on Whisper transcripts, THEN downstream outputs may inherit mistakes.
mitigations: Review transcripts before reuse.
Mark Whisper output as unverified.
Ask ChatGPT Desktop to cite exact transcript spans.
Use a second pass for critical audio.
requires-engineering: add automated transcript-confidence gating.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Whisper touches audio/speech. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, and Whisper is local/network-none. The main compliance issue is limited to handling sensitive audio through a vendor-backed desktop app, so the blast radius is narrower than medium.
conditions: IF regulated audio is transcribed and then moved into ChatGPT Desktop, THEN policy obligations may apply.
IF the operator requires local-only processing for a data class, THEN ChatGPT Desktop may violate that requirement.
mitigations: Keep regulated audio out of ChatGPT Desktop.
Use local-only transcription for restricted data.
Document the data flow before processing.
Delete temporary transcripts promptly.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to the workflow.
